# Section 1: Overview

# Purpose
The purpose of this document is to provide a detailed and testable specification for implementing the Holding Company hierarchy, centralized user administration, permission control, and finance transaction enablement across member companies.
The document is intended for product owners, business analysts, architects, developers, QA teams, configuration teams, and implementation teams who must align on scope, user behavior, screen changes, validations, and acceptance criteria.
This document defines the business and functional requirements for enhancing the existing organizational structure and enabling controlled cross-company transaction processing under a Holding Company model.

# Business Requirement:
The business requires a scalable organization model in which one Holding Company can govern multiple Member Companies without losing company-level operational control.
Central administrators must be able to create users, assign permissions, and manage visibility across the organizational hierarchy from a single control point.
Finance users must be able to perform approved cross-company processes with clear company, division, and branch identification at header and detail level where applicable.
The solution must maintain auditability, role-based access, and clear segregation between visibility control and transactional ownership.
Currently, the system operates on a Company–Division level hierarchy, where all transactions and operations are managed within divisions under a company.

# Scope
This scope includes organization setup, hierarchy visualization, user-group and permission management, finance feature enablement, holding-level governance, member-company maintenance, and reporting structures for divisions and branches.
The scope also includes all referenced screens that compare existing and proposed behavior. Every screen included in this document must be treated as a requirement artifact and must be explained by purpose, user action, expected outcome, and validation points.

## Holding Company
This section explains the rights and responsibilities of a Holding (Group) Company and the users created under it. The Holding Company works as a central control layer for multiple Member Companies, allowing centralized user management, permission control, reporting, and finance governance.
The Holding Company does not represent a separate legal operating entity for day-to-day transactional posting. Instead, it provides visibility, configuration control, permission administration, and coordinated oversight across all linked member companies.
• User creation and access management
• Company, division, and branch location permissions
• Program and report access across all member companies
• Finance governance, including master data management
• Intercompany transaction visibility and elimination

# Section 2. Assumptions
The following assumptions apply to this enhancement:
The existing company, division, branch, user, and permission masters remain available and are extended rather than redesigned from scratch.
The Holding Company is a logical governance layer and does not replace the legal ownership of transactions by the respective Member Company.
Only authorized configuration or administrative users can create or modify organization hierarchy records and permission mappings.
All new fields introduced in headers or grids must follow standard audit logging, validation, and role-based visibility controls already used in the application.
Where current screens are retained, existing approved functions must continue to work unless an explicit change is documented in this specification.
• Assumptions are expanded in the section above.

# Section 3. Solution

# Functional Requirements

## 3.1 Global Company (Holding Company) and Member Company Hierarchy Setup.
Detailed requirement: The system shall support a parent-child hierarchy in which one logical Holding Company can contain multiple Member Companies, and each Member Company can contain one or more Divisions and Branches as applicable.
Setup sequence must follow a controlled order: create Holding Company, create Member Company, create Division, create Branch, map defaults, assign users, and then activate the required permissions and finance features.
The setup process must validate uniqueness of group code, company code, currency configuration, and active status before the organization record is saved.
A complete hierarchy must be visible immediately after setup so that authorized users can confirm the structural relationship from the top node to the lowest operational node.
When a new organization is set up in the system, the business team shares the required information with the Configuration Team. Based on these inputs, the Configuration Team manually creates the Global Company(Holding Company) and the associated Member Company.
Note: The Holding Company is a logical control layer in the application. It is used for governance, reporting visibility, centralized permissions, and finance enablement, but it is not treated as a separate physical or legal entity for operational postings.
The following details are provided for company creation:
• Company Name
• Company Short Name
• Company Currency
• Reporting Currency
• Enable Base FA Integration (Yes/No)
• Enable FA (Yes/No)
• Is Asmara Model (Yes/No)
• Member Company Code (e.g., 76670)
Global (Holding) Company Details: In addition to the above member company information, the following details are required to create the Global (Holding) Company:
• Group Name
• Group Code
• Group Functional Currency
• Group Reporting Currency
• Group Financial Year.
• Group active/Inactive
Once the company setup is completed and the user logs into the system, the organizational structure hierarchy should be displayed, as shown in the screen below.
Note: User need to create “Division” and “Branch” after creation of Member company.
Figure 1. Screen reference - 3.1 Global Company (Holding Company) and Member Company Hierarchy Setup. - Note: User need to create “Division” and “Branch” after creation of Member company.
This screenshot supports the requirement context for 3.1 Global Company (Holding Company) and Member Company Hierarchy Setup. - Note: User need to create “Division” and “Branch” after creation of Member company.. Reviewers should verify the visible fields, tab structure, action controls, selection behavior, and any company, division, branch, or permission indicators shown in this screen.

## 3.2 Org. Structure New Screen View
Screen objective: Provide a single operational view of the organizational hierarchy with enough information for administrators to understand ownership, default assignments, security context, and downstream permission impact.
The screen shall show hierarchy nodes in expandable tree format and support clear visual separation between Holding Company, Member Company, Division, Branch, user groups, and users.
The new columns Default Member Company, Default Division, and Default Branch shall be visible where relevant and shall indicate the primary assignment used for login context, permission resolution, and transaction defaults.
If a user has access to multiple nodes, the default values shall drive the initial landing context while still allowing the user to switch to other authorized nodes according to role permissions.
The hierarchy is used to organize Member company users, roles, division, sites, and branch in a clear and structured way. It helps in managing access, responsibilities, and reporting across the organization. The hierarchy follows a tree structure, where higher-level entities contain lower-level units.
Figure 2. Screen reference - 3.2 Org. Structure New Screen View - The hierarchy is used to organize Member company users, roles, division, sites, and branch in a clear and structured way

### Permissions Tab Screens
All permission-related screens in this section must be interpreted with the same rule set: each screen shall clearly show the permission object, access scope, level of control, and impact on user behavior after save.
Every permission screen should explain who can maintain it, what business area it controls, what entities are affected, and whether the change is immediate or requires refresh, re-login, or reauthorization.

#### Program Permission Tab
• Used to manage access to different system programs or modules.
• Controls what functional areas are visible to the user.
• This screen is used to define detailed, role-based access control.
• Permissions can be applied at program, menu, and action level.
• Copy and paste options reduce manual work and errors.
• Dropdowns help define approval authority and access type clearly.

## 3.3 Master Configuration for Enabling FA Transactions
This section defines the master configuration screen used by authorized administrators to enable or disable FA transaction visibility by level, module, menu, and sub-menu item.
The master screen is a control screen only. It does not create transactional data; instead, it governs whether a specific feature is visible and available at Holding Company level, Member Company level, or both.
Changes made in this master must be auditable and must not grant access beyond the user's own administration scope.
Path: Admin > Global Setup
The purpose of this screen is to centrally control the visibility of all menu-based features across the entire application. This is a master configuration screen where no data entry or structural editing is allowed. All menu names, grouping, and permission levels are pre-defined and pre-filled.
The only action you perform here is to Enable or Disable a feature using the toggle switch in the ENABLE column.
Once disabled, the feature is completely hidden from all users under the applicable permission level. Once enabled, it becomes visible and accessible again. This screen is typically accessible only to Holding Company level administrators, and the changes affect either Holding Company users, Member Company users, or both — depending on the pre-set Visibility level.
• While creating user there will be a facility to mark a user as Holding Company this will be given by super admin to normal admin.
• Holding company user can grant or revoke any permission.
• All user of any member company will be created in holding company.
• There will be a setup for FA/Inventory master configuration, whether these menu will be visibilie to Holding Company or for Member Company.
• Holding Company user will give permission of Member Company, Division & Locations.

## 3.4 Holding Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement
This section defines holding-level user administration, access control behavior, and finance enablement rules that apply when a user is created under the Holding Company governance layer.
This scope defines the functional coverage for Holding (Group) Company–level users, permissions, finance controls, reporting visibility, and intercompany governance across all linked Member Companies

### 3.4.1 Centralized User Creation and Identity Management at Holding Company Level
Holding-level user creation shall support centralized identity management while still enforcing organization-specific visibility through default member company, division, and branch mapping.
A holding-level user may have visibility across multiple entities, but access must still be constrained by explicit permission assignment and approved company mapping.
Mandatory defaults shall be validated during user creation so that a user always has a valid initial organization context at login.
The Holding Company does not exist as a physical or legal entity in the system. It is a logical control layer, enabled by marking specific administrators as Holding (Group) Company Users, who are responsible for managing users, permissions, masters, and crosscompany governance
All users in the system will be created, maintained, and governed at the Holding (Group) Company level. User creation at the group level ensures centralized control, consistent permission management, and standardized access across all linked Member Companies. The Holding Company acts as the single point of user administration, while actual operational access is controlled through permissions assigned during or after user creation.
• Only authorized administrators at the Holding Company level can create users even there are other admin.
• Users will not be created independently at the Member Company level.
• Any changes to user details, defaults, or access rights must be performed from the Holding Company context.

#### Default Member Company (Mandatory)
• Each user must be mapped to one default Member Company.
• This default company defines:
• The user’s initial landing context after login
• The default company selected when opening reports or transactions
• Assigning a default Member Company does not restrict the user to that company alone.
• Actual company access depends on the Member Company permissions granted separately.

#### Default Division (Mandatory)
• A default Division must be selected for each user.
• This division serves as:
• The starting operational unit for the user
• A reference for data filtering and transaction initiation
• If the user is assigned multiple divisions later, the default division will be used as the initial selection.
Figure 88. Screen reference - Default Division (Mandatory) - If the user is assigned multiple divisions later, the default division will be used as the initial selection.

### 3.4.2 Holding Company F/A Transactions
All finance transactions initiated under holding-level visibility must still clearly identify the operational company, division, and branch responsible for the transaction and posting result.
Where the same screen supports cross-company processing, the system shall require explicit line-level ownership and preserve posting traceability for each affected company.

#### Expense Invoice
Detailed requirement for Expense Invoice: the transaction header shall clearly capture Company, Division, and Branch according to the user's authorized scope and configured defaults.
Where split posting is supported, line-level distribution must preserve company ownership, ledger mapping, branch impact, and a complete audit trail for each line.
The system shall prevent save or posting if mandatory organization fields are blank, inconsistent, inactive, or not permitted for the logged-in user.
• Introduce Company, Division, and Branch selection fields on the header
• Only Those company, Division and branch need to be shown for which user have permission.
• These fields are mandatory to select
• Default values should show the logged-in user’s member Company, Division, and Branch.
• Note: - Branch need to be shown only when Unit accounting is enabled.
Figure 92. Screen reference - Expense Invoice - Note: - Branch need to be shown only when Unit accounting is enabled.
This screenshot supports the requirement context for Expense Invoice - Note: - Branch need to be shown only when Unit accounting is enabled.. Reviewers should verify the visible fields, tab structure, action controls, selection behavior, and any company, division, branch, or permission indicators shown in this screen.
• If the user selects General Expense as the Invoice Type, then in the Expense tab (as shown in the attached image):
• Provide selection options for Company, Division, Branch, and an Amount column
• User should be able to split the ledger amount across multiple Company lines
• System must ensure the total of split amounts equals the original ledger amount

## 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement
This section defines the behavior for users created and maintained at Member Company level, including required defaults, access control boundaries, and finance transactions available within approved organizational scope.
A Member Company is an individual legal entity within the group where all daytoday financial activities are carried out. It is mandatory for transaction entry, user access control, and companylevel reporting. All finance transactions such as invoices, vouchers, payments, tax postings, and adjustments are recorded at the member company level, with mandatory company selection on every transaction. User access, menu permissions, and report visibility are also controlled companywise to ensure data security and segregation. Masters like accounts, vendors, customers, cost centers, and buyers can be centrally created and mapped to the member company for consistency. If branch accounting is enabled, branch selection becomes compulsory, with flexibility to allocate a single transaction across multiple branches and other dimensions such as cost centers and buyer orders. This structure ensures operational flexibility while maintaining strong financial control and accurate reporting.
A Member Company is:
• A legal entity under a group
• Used for actual transaction entry
• Used for access control and reporting
Each member company can have:
• Its own users
• Its own division
• Its own branches
• Its own transactions

### 3.5.1 Fields to create a member company
Member Company creation must capture sufficient master data to support legal identity, reporting alignment, transaction control, activation status, and future hierarchy expansion.
All required fields must be validated before activation, and duplicate company code or conflicting reporting configuration must be rejected.

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 10 rows · columns: Field (text), Meaning (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Meaning |
| Group Name | Select parent group |
| Group Code | Auto-fetched (system-controlled) |
| Company Name / Code | Legal entity identity |
| Group Reporting Currency | Auto (group-level currency) |
| Group Financial Year | Auto-aligned with group |
| Company Active/Inactive | Enable/Disable transactions |
| Company Level Address (No GSTIN) | Legal address without tax complexity |
| Logo | Company branding |
| Flexi Fields | Custom company attributes |
| Ledger Name (Optional) | If company is also treated as a ledger |

### 3.5.2 Member Company F/A Transactions
Member Company finance transactions must operate within the user's authorized company scope while preserving the same field-level clarity and posting traceability expected at holding level.

#### Expense Invoice
Detailed requirement for Expense Invoice: the transaction header shall clearly capture Company, Division, and Branch according to the user's authorized scope and configured defaults.
Where split posting is supported, line-level distribution must preserve company ownership, ledger mapping, branch impact, and a complete audit trail for each line.
The system shall prevent save or posting if mandatory organization fields are blank, inconsistent, inactive, or not permitted for the logged-in user.
• Introduce Company, Division, and Branch fields on the header
• Company and Division fields will be freeze for member company
• Only those branch need to be shown for which user have permission.
• These fields are mandatory to select.
• Default values should show the logged-in user’s member Company, Division, and Branch.
• Note: Branch need to be shown only when Unit Accounting is enabled.

## 3.6 Division Reporting structure under the member company.
Division reporting must provide a clear intermediate layer under the Member Company for operational segregation, reporting visibility, default assignment, and transaction routing where business processes are division-specific.
The reporting structure must allow users and reports to identify which division owns a transaction, approval chain, and reporting result.
Under the Member Company, a Division is maintained only for reporting and analysis and does not affect transaction posting in any way, transaction will be made at Branch Level. Divisions help users view financial data in a structured, divisionwise manner across all finance screens. When a user has access to a single division, only transactions related to that division will be visible to them. Divisions can be reused across other legal entities using a copy option to maintain consistency in reporting. Each division is defined using basic identifiers such as division name, code, prefix, and optional flexi fields, and is intended purely to support management and reporting views.
Figure 166. Screen reference - 3.6 Division Reporting structure under the member company. - Under the Member Company, a Division is maintained only for reporting and analysis and does not affect transaction posti
This screenshot supports the requirement context for 3.6 Division Reporting structure under the member company. - Under the Member Company, a Division is maintained only for reporting and analysis and does not affect transaction posti. Reviewers should verify the visible fields, tab structure, action controls, selection behavior, and any company, division, branch, or permission indicators shown in this screen.

# Section 4. Acceptance Criteria
The enhancement shall be considered acceptable only when the following criteria are met:
A Holding Company can be created, linked to one or more Member Companies, and displayed correctly in the hierarchy tree.
Default Member Company, Default Division, and Default Branch are visible and correctly applied for authorized users wherever defined in this specification.
All permission tabs display the correct scope and only show options that the administrator is authorized to maintain.
FA feature visibility follows the master configuration and does not expose unauthorized menus or actions.
Transaction screens capture company ownership clearly and support valid posting, audit trail, and reporting traceability.
All screenshots referenced in this document are attached, captioned, and explained so that business, technical, and QA teams can interpret the intended behavior without ambiguity.

## 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.
Branch reporting must extend the hierarchy below the division or member company as configured, allowing operational location-level visibility, assignment, and reporting without breaking the parent-child relationship of the hierarchy.
Branch display and selection must follow the unit accounting enablement rules and should only appear where the feature is allowed by configuration.
• A Branch represents a physical business location, such as MNB – Bangalore, with complete address details
• Branches are created under a Division and reflect where actual operational activities take place
• Branch accounting can be enabled or disabled at the system level
• Branch will be there on the header of all the finance screens
• When branch accounting is enabled:
• Branch becomes mandatory on the header of all finance screens
• User access can be restricted to specific branches
• Users can view and create transactions only for their permitted branches
• Transactions for all permitted branches should be visible automatically, without requiring branch switching
• Each branch is defined using the following details:
• Branch Name
• Branch Code
• Complete address information
• Branch Ledger (mandatory if branch accounting is enabled, optional otherwise)
• Default cost center (single or multiple cost categories, as required)
Figure 167. Screen reference - 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company. - Default cost center (single or multiple cost categories, as required)
This screenshot supports the requirement context for 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company. - Default cost center (single or multiple cost categories, as required). Reviewers should verify the visible fields, tab structure, action controls, selection behavior, and any company, division, branch, or permission indicators shown in this screen.

# Section 4. Acceptance Criteria and Business Scenarios
Additional acceptance checks for branch reporting and downstream scenarios are defined below.

## Business Scenarios
Scenario 1: A holding-level administrator creates a new user, assigns default member company, division, and branch, and confirms that the user sees only the approved hierarchy and menus after login.
Scenario 2: A permission administrator updates a program permission tab and confirms that only the selected modules, menus, and actions become available to the target user group.
Scenario 3: A finance user creates a transaction involving company-specific posting lines and verifies that every line retains the correct company and branch ownership in posting and reporting.
Scenario 4: A member-company user performs the same activity with limited access and confirms that holding-only controls are not visible.
Scenario 5: A branch-enabled organization confirms that branch selection is shown only when unit accounting rules permit it.

CANDIDATES FOR REVIEW (possible definitions, formulas, validations, steps; not confirmed knowledge)
- definition (§ Purpose): The purpose of this document is to provide a detailed and testable specification for implementing the Holding Company hierarchy, centralized user administration, permission control, and finance transaction enablement across member companies.
- definition (§ Purpose): The document is intended for product owners, business analysts, architects, developers, QA teams, configuration teams, and implementation teams who must align on scope, user behavior, screen changes, validations, and acceptance criteria.
- validation (§ Purpose): The document is intended for product owners, business analysts, architects, developers, QA teams, configuration teams, and implementation teams who must align on scope, user behavior, screen changes, validations, and acceptance criteria.
- validation (§ Business Requirement:): Central administrators must be able to create users, assign permissions, and manage visibility across the organizational hierarchy from a single control point.
- validation (§ Business Requirement:): Finance users must be able to perform approved cross-company processes with clear company, division, and branch identification at header and detail level where applicable.
- validation (§ Business Requirement:): The solution must maintain auditability, role-based access, and clear segregation between visibility control and transactional ownership.
- validation (§ Scope): Every screen included in this document must be treated as a requirement artifact and must be explained by purpose, user action, expected outcome, and validation points.
- workflow_steps (§ Scope › Holding Company): Holding Company: / 1. User creation and access management / 2. Company, division, and branch location permissions / 3. Program and report access across all member companies / 4. Finance governance, including master data management / 5. Intercompany transaction visibility and elimination
- definition (§ Section 2. Assumptions): The Holding Company is a logical governance layer and does not replace the legal ownership of transactions by the respective Member Company.
- validation (§ Section 2. Assumptions): All new fields introduced in headers or grids must follow standard audit logging, validation, and role-based visibility controls already used in the application.
- definition (§ Section 2. Assumptions): Where current screens are retained, existing approved functions must continue to work unless an explicit change is documented in this specification.
- validation (§ Section 2. Assumptions): Where current screens are retained, existing approved functions must continue to work unless an explicit change is documented in this specification.
- definition (§ Section 2. Assumptions): Assumptions are expanded in the section above.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.1 Global Company (Holding Company) and Member Company Hierarchy Setup.): Setup sequence must follow a controlled order: create Holding Company, create Member Company, create Division, create Branch, map defaults, assign users, and then activate the required permissions and finance features.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.1 Global Company (Holding Company) and Member Company Hierarchy Setup.): The setup process must validate uniqueness of group code, company code, currency configuration, and active status before the organization record is saved.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.1 Global Company (Holding Company) and Member Company Hierarchy Setup.): A complete hierarchy must be visible immediately after setup so that authorized users can confirm the structural relationship from the top node to the lowest operational node.

- definition (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): A Member Company is an individual legal entity within the group where all daytoday financial activities are carried out.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): It is mandatory for transaction entry, user access control, and companylevel reporting.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): It is mandatory for transaction entry, user access control, and companylevel reporting.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): All finance transactions such as invoices, vouchers, payments, tax postings, and adjustments are recorded at the member company level, with mandatory company selection on every transaction.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): If branch accounting is enabled, branch selection becomes compulsory, with flexibility to allocate a single transaction across multiple branches and other dimensions such as cost centers and buyer orders.
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement: / 1. A legal entity under a group / 2. Used for actual transaction entry / 3. Used for access control and reporting
- workflow_steps (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement): 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement: / 1. Its own users / 2. Its own division / 3. Its own branches / 4. Its own transactions
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement › 3.5.1 Fields to create a member company): Member Company creation must capture sufficient master data to support legal identity, reporting alignment, transaction control, activation status, and future hierarchy expansion.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement › 3.5.1 Fields to create a member company): All required fields must be validated before activation, and duplicate company code or conflicting reporting configuration must be rejected.
- table (§ Functional Requirements › 3.5 Member Company User Management, Access Control, and Finance Enablement › 3.5.1 Fields to create a member company, table 3): Table 3: Field, Meaning (10 rows; identifiers: Field)

Only those branch need to be shown for which user have permission. / 4. These fields are mandatory to select. / 5. Default values should show the logged-in user’s member Company, Division, and Branch. / 6. Note: Branch need to be shown only when Unit Accounting is enabled.

- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.6 Division Reporting structure under the member company.): Division reporting must provide a clear intermediate layer under the Member Company for operational segregation, reporting visibility, default assignment, and transaction routing where business processes are division-specific.
- validation (§ Functional Requirements › 3.6 Division Reporting structure under the member company.): The reporting structure must allow users and reports to identify which division owns a transaction, approval chain, and reporting result.
- definition (§ Functional Requirements › 3.6 Division Reporting structure under the member company.): Each division is defined using basic identifiers such as division name, code, prefix, and optional flexi fields, and is intended purely to support management and reporting views.
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria): The enhancement shall be considered acceptable only when the following criteria are met:
- definition (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria): All screenshots referenced in this document are attached, captioned, and explained so that business, technical, and QA teams can interpret the intended behavior without ambiguity.
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Branch reporting must extend the hierarchy below the division or member company as configured, allowing operational location-level visibility, assignment, and reporting without breaking the parent-child relationship of the hierarchy.
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Branch display and selection must follow the unit accounting enablement rules and should only appear where the feature is allowed by configuration.
- definition (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): A Branch represents a physical business location, such as MNB – Bangalore, with complete address details
- definition (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Branches are created under a Division and reflect where actual operational activities take place
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Branch becomes mandatory on the header of all finance screens
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): User access can be restricted to specific branches
- definition (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Each branch is defined using the following details:
- definition (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Branch Ledger (mandatory if branch accounting is enabled, optional otherwise)
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): Branch Ledger (mandatory if branch accounting is enabled, optional otherwise)
- workflow_steps (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria › 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.): 3.7 Branch Reporting structure under the member company.: / 1. A Branch represents a physical business location, such as MNB – Bangalore, with complete address details / 2. Branches are created under a Division and reflect where actual operational activities take place / 3. Branch accounting can be enabled or disabled at the system level / 4. Branch will be there on the header of all the finance screens / 5. When branch accounting is enabled: / 6. Branch becomes mandatory on the header of all finance screens / 7. User access can be restricted to specific branches / 8. Users can view and create transactions only for their permitted branches / 9. Transactions for all permitted branches should be visible automatically, without requiring branch switching / 10. Each branch is defined using the following details: / 11. Branch Name / 12. Branch Code / 13. Complete address information / 14. Branch Ledger (mandatory if branch accounting is enabled, optional otherwise) / 15. Default cost center (single or multiple cost categories, as required)
- validation (§ Section 4. Acceptance Criteria and Business Scenarios › Business Scenarios): Scenario 5: A branch-enabled organization confirms that branch selection is shown only when unit accounting rules permit it.
